name: brainDB project brain
goal: Ship 0.0.3 with the paraphrase question answered by a measurement, SQLite behind the storage interface, and no silent behaviour change for 0.0.2 brains

memories.text: The README calls the project status a concept: commands, BDQL syntax, config keys, API endpoints and performance numbers are a specification to react to, not a stable contract, and breaking changes are expected at every 0.0.x step. The current version is 0.0.2
The whole brain is memory; only the lit slice is the working context. The slice comes from spreading activation that starts at a focus and runs to a chosen depth
Weight curve since 0.0.2: w = base * (floor + (1 - floor) * 0.5^(age / half-life)), multiplied by 0.3 when superseded. Pinned memories do not decay and BOOST resets the clock
Activation spreads level by level: a(v) = a(u) * w(u,v) * hop * (0.35 + 0.65 * w(v)), kept while it stays at or above the threshold, up to depth

Decay defaults after 0.0.2: decision 365 d floor 0.80, fact 180 d floor 0.70, record 180 d floor 0.70, file 180 d floor 0.60, chunk 120 d floor 0.55, summary 90 d floor 0.40, idea 60 d floor 0.25; task 14 d, question 7 d and note 7 d keep floor 0 and really do go away

Nodes come in two classes: knowledge nodes (memories, records, chunks, concepts) cost tokens and appear in the context; connector nodes (anchor, bridge, hub, alias, time) hold no knowledge, never appear as results and cost no tokens, but activation and search route through them

Four search modes: hybrid (vector seeds then graph activation), vector (kNN over graph-enriched embeddings), tree (beam search over the graph) and graph (word stems plus activation, which also reaches knowledge findable only through connections)
The built-in hash-256 engine indexes 5-letter stems, bigrams and character trigrams. It is lexical retrieval in vector clothing: offline, deterministic, free, and blind to synonyms

Graph activation ranks best overall of the four search modes. Measured 20 Nov 2026, brainDB 0.0.2, Go 1.27.4, hash-256 dim 256, 144 nodes, k = 10, 32 hand-judged queries over examples/sales-company: graph MRR 0.57 and nDCG@10 0.52, vector MRR 0.46 and nDCG@10 0.44, hybrid 0.47 / 0.44, tree 0.47 / 0.47

The paraphrase collapse: on the 16 queries that share only meaning with their target, 12 to 14 of 16 return nothing relevant in the top ten, in every mode. Activation can only spread from seeds that similarity found, and with hash-256 similarity finds nothing

On the 16 lexical queries, graph mode puts a relevant memory first every single time: MRR 1.00, nDCG@10 0.91, no query without a hit. That is the measured evidence for the graph-activation design claim

Only four paraphrases found anything at all, and they found it through the graph rather than through similarity: 'will the units survive hot conditions' at rank 1, 'yearly revenue from our most important client' at 6, 'smallest profit we are allowed to accept' at 8, 'why we cannot meet the lower competing offer' at 10
Latency and scale are not measured at all. Every throughput and response-time figure in README and SPEC Addendum F6 is a design target
A brain is stored today as one brain.xml file, written atomically, human-readable and diff-friendly, with a lossless round trip, and every change is appended to brain.journal.jsonl
Embeddings are enriched over the graph with APPNP: h = (1 - alpha) * x + alpha * mean_w(neighbours), so a node's vector carries its neighbourhood

embedding.provider: openai sends text to any OpenAI-compatible /embeddings endpoint: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM or a local Text Embeddings Inference server. One config block, no provider SDK, no code change

Embedding requests are batched (default 64), retried on 429 and 5xx with capped exponential backoff, and cached on disk by sha256(model + text) in embeddings.cache next to the brain, so restarts and re-imports cost no API calls and changing the model invalidates the cache by itself
API keys are referenced by environment-variable name only. No key is ever written to braindb.yaml, brain.xml or the embedding cache, and a missing apiKeyEnv variable is an error at load time
Environment overrides for the embedding engine: BRAINDB_EMBED_PROVIDER, _MODEL, _BASE_URL, _KEY_ENV, _DIM, _FALLBACK, _CACHE. They make an eval run against a different engine a one-line change

Access labels switch whole areas of the brain off for a user without clearance: no context, no traversal, no search hits, and no leak through vectors, scores, counts, connectors or error messages. A property test guarantees the non-leakage

Every brain has a purpose in braindb.yaml, and every incoming item is scored against it deterministically and with reasons, then admitted, quarantined for review or rejected. Agents receive the purpose with their context, so they know what to store

The MCP server exposes two tools by default, brain_view and brain_run, and every reply ends with a status line carrying lit size, tokens, depth and focus. The full tool set (view, search, inspect, query, fill, exec, ingest, sources) is opened per database in braindb.yaml

Imports are incremental: unchanged files are skipped, changed files supersede the previous version instead of duplicating it. Tables become kinds, rows become records, foreign keys become links and low-cardinality columns become concepts

Entities are recognised in every text and record, normalised (dates to ISO 8601, money to an ISO 4217 amount, phones to E.164) and indexed in several locales, then used for filters, search boosts, template slots and RESOLVE anchors. Card numbers are always masked
Federation is partial: sources and external stubs are stored and linkable as lab:f101, but the remote transports and federated search are still planned
braindb publish (a brain compiled into one executable that is an MCP server when run with no arguments) and snapshots are planned, not built

Automatic bridge and time connectors are planned, and the config keys connectors.bridges and connectors.time are rejected by the loader so they cannot silently do nothing. Bridges can still be created by hand with CONNECTOR bridge, and time is queried through the touched column
The core is a single static Go binary with the web UI embedded and no runtime dependencies. The core is stdlib-only; SQLite will be the one dependency the project takes
The web UI carries 119 Vitest unit tests over src/model with 75% statement coverage, and every component has a Storybook story. Components are covered by stories, pure modules by tests
brainDB is Apache-2.0 with a NOTICE file; the author is Gabriel Koziestanski, and the version banner prints the attribution

Examples that ship: sales-company (B2B sales), research-lab (electrolyte development), import-demo (a raw pile turned into a database by one braindb create), federation (sales mounting the lab) and braindb-self (this brain)
The gold set is rejected at load time when a relevant id does not exist in the brain, because a typo in a gold file otherwise shows up as a retrieval failure and quietly lowers every score
Relevance in the gold set is binary and deliberately tight: only memories that actually answer the query are judged relevant, and the reasoning for each paraphrase is recorded in its note field
Purpose admission enforces by default: items scoring below the accept threshold are dropped at the door

Purpose admission defaults to advise, not enforce. Silently dropping knowledge because a similarity score fell below a threshold is an invisible, unrecoverable loss; enforce is opt-in and every shipped example uses advise
Weights follow a plain half-life curve and every kind fades to zero with age (0.0.1 policy: decision 60 d, fact 30 d, file 14 d)

Decay no longer deletes knowledge. Every kind carries a floor, the share of its base weight that age can never take away; durable kinds rank lower with age but stay in the graph, and only SUPERSEDE and FORGET remove knowledge
Build the storage engine by hand: a custom write-ahead log, inverted and range indexes, a query planner, a pure-Go HNSW index and a from-scratch Redis client

SQLite replaces the hand-rolled storage engine and is the one dependency the project will take, because it already provides the WAL, the indexes, the planner, concurrent readers and crash safety. Redis is off the roadmap and docker-compose.redis.yml is removed

The embedding engine is pluggable and hash-256 stays the default, so nothing changes unless it is configured; fallback: hash degrades and reports the engine as degraded, fallback: error fails the operation instead
Performance figures are labelled as targets everywhere in the documentation, because none of them has been measured
No emoji anywhere in the repository (Addendum N). Icons are inline SVG, and TestNoEmoji fails the build on a stray glyph

CI gates on every push and pull request: gofmt -l must be empty, then go vet, go test -race, go build, then npm ci, typecheck, the web unit tests, the emoji lint, the Vite build and the Storybook build. make test mirrors the same checks locally

Retrieval quality is reported with its caveats in the open: docs/BENCHMARKS.md states which questions are measured, which are not, and that 32 queries over a 64-memory fictional brain is a smoke test, not a benchmark

The documented default engine for general agent use must change: hash-256 stays the right default for offline and zero-cost work, but any question phrased in a user's own words needs a real embedding model, so the README default guidance is reopened for 0.0.3
A brain's own project knowledge ships as an example (this one), so the agent working on brainDB reads decisions and measurements out of a brain instead of re-reading 3,400 lines of documentation

Run braindb eval with openai/text-embedding-3-small through OpenRouter and fill the two empty rows of the engine table in docs/BENCHMARKS.md, including the vector-only control that isolates embeddings from graph activation
Put SQLite behind the storage-engine interface from Addendum F1 and keep brain.xml as an export format, not as the hot path
Implement the remote transports for federation sources so that SEARCH ... SOURCES lab and SELECT ... FROM memory@lab reach a live server instead of a stored stub
Build braindb publish: embed the brain, precompute the indices, ship read-only, overlay and writable modes
Decide and implement automatic bridge and time connectors, or drop the two rejected config keys from the loader
Grow the gold set past 32 queries and add an agent-shaped bucket: questions an assistant asks mid-task, not questions a person types into a search box
Say in the README quick start, not only in BENCHMARKS, that the default engine does not match paraphrases
Add braindb-self to the example lists in internal/brain/brain_test.go and internal/brain/importer_test.go so the seed and the config are validated by go test
Measure latency and scale with braindb bench on both backends and replace the Addendum F6 targets with results
Keep one stats fixture per storage backend in Storybook; the Redis-shaped fixtures are why the file-backend crash reached a release
Does a real embedding model fix the paraphrase collapse, or is part of it a graph problem? The experiment is one command away and needs an API key
Should hash-256 stay the documented default once a measured alternative exists, given that every agent use case phrases questions in the user's own words?
How much of any improvement comes from the embeddings and how much from graph activation on top of them? The remote vector-only row is the control that answers it
What moves to SQLite first: the node store, the entity index, or the vectors?
Which transport should federated search use between two brains, the HTTP API or MCP over Streamable HTTP?
How is a published brain assembled into an executable without a Go toolchain on the publishing machine?
How many judged queries are enough to rank two good engines against each other, rather than to show a collapse?
Without enforce, how does an agent decide what is worth remembering: the advise score, the purpose text, or a rule in the procedure?
What exactly changes for a 0.0.1 brain on upgrade? Content is kept, but weights and therefore ranking and context change on the next load
Is the lit slice at depth 2 the right default for an agent's first turn, or should the first turn be depth 1 with an explicit widen?
The emoji lint caught the navigation glyph in docs/index.html; it is an inline SVG now
The web unit tests found a real bug while being written: a typed kind: prefix and a kind chip were ORed instead of ANDed in browseFilter, so kind:task with the fact chip on showed both
The parity fixture against the JavaScript prototype pins LegacyDecay() explicitly, because parity is about the algorithms, not about which half-life ships today
Three bugs in 0.0.2 were the same shape: a Go nil slice marshalled to JSON null, optional server fields typed as required in TypeScript. whoami roles, stats indexes and latency, the wizard dry run
index.html is served no-cache and the hashed assets under /assets/ immutable, after a browser kept a stale index that named assets which no longer existed

Agent loop on this brain: start with CONTEXT FOR the question at depth 1, read the status line for lit size and tokens, widen to depth 2 only if the answer is not in the slice; after a decision is made, REMEMBER it as kind decision and LINK it to the question it answers; retire the old version with SUPERSEDE, never FORGET

Release checklist: CHANGELOG entry that says which behaviour changes, make test green, make eval re-run and its date and engine recorded in docs/BENCHMARKS.md, docs/index.html kept in parity with README, every example still loading under go test

Adding an example: seed.json, braindb.yaml, docs/ to ingest, templates/, queries.bdql and a README with the numbers from a real run; then add the name to the example lists in the Go tests so a broken seed fails CI

Measuring retrieval: seed a clean brain, run braindb eval --gold with the bucket split, and record engine, dimension, node count, k and date next to every number. A number without its engine is not a result

Cheap BDQL: project the columns you need with SELECT instead of reading whole memories, filter by kind and section before NEAR, let connectors carry the joins, and keep depth at 2 unless a path test says otherwise
Publish this brain as an MCP binary with every release, so an agent can mount the brainDB manual as a read-only source instead of fetching documentation pages
A purpose-score column in the Browse tab would show what advise mode would have dropped, which is the evidence needed before anyone turns enforce on
braindb skill install could drop skills/braindb-bdql into a project's agent configuration, so the agent writes BDQL from the cheat sheet instead of guessing
An eval bucket of questions taken from real agent transcripts would measure the thing the project is for, instead of the thing that is easy to judge
Addendum A: the context brain as a database. Records hold structured raw data, A2 is the raw data query, A3 the context query, A4 template fill, A5 the interfaces
Addendum B: publish a brain as a compiled MCP binary, with the brain embedded and its indices precomputed, and no Go toolchain needed at publish time
Addendum C: external sources and federation. C1 sources, C2 external links, C3 federated operations, C4 interfaces, C5 the worked example
Addendum D: the UI as a professional database tool, with a navigator tree, a tabbed workspace, an inspector and a status bar
Addendum E: creating databases from bulk imports and configuring a brain. E1 multiple databases, E2 bulk import, E3 braindb.yaml, E4 UI, E5 tests, E6 the import-demo example
Addendum F: performance at scale, storage and embedding providers. F1 the storage engine interface, F2 the SQLite schema, F6 the performance targets, F8 the implemented embedding providers
Addendum G: BDQL, the brainDB query language. G1 statements, G2 results, G3 transactions and safety, G4 interfaces, G5 implementation notes, G6 grammar completeness
Addendum H: connector nodes, structural and knowledge-free. Types anchor, bridge, hub, alias and time; activation passes through a bridge without spending a depth level
Addendum I: the built-in pattern library, written as Go RE2 regexps so there is no catastrophic backtracking
Addendum J: remote MCP over Streamable HTTP with scoped tokens
Addendum K: license and attribution. Apache-2.0, with a NOTICE file and the attribution printed by the version banner
Addendum L: storage formats, readable XML and a fast versioned little-endian binary .bdb, with conversion tools and targets measured by braindb bench --format bin|xml
Addendum M: users, roles, grants and access-controlled knowledge. M2 states the non-leakage guarantees, which are the core requirement and are property-tested
Addendum N: icons, no emoji
Addendum O: brain purpose and the admission pre-filter, with the configuration in O1

retrieval: Flat top-k over chunks, no graph
decay: Everything fades to zero after 90 days
Pinning as the only way to keep a fact
Linear decay instead of a half-life
embeddings: Bundled ONNX runtime for local models
Vectors stored outside the brain file
mcp: One tool per operation, twelve tools
Tool output without a status line
federation: Copying a remote brain into the local one
access: Row filtering in the UI only
purpose: A hand-written allow list of topics
ui: A single stats fixture for every backend
benchmark: A gold set without a paraphrase bucket
agentmem: Dumping the whole brain into the prompt
A fixed system prompt instead of a focus

connectors.label: the paraphrase collapse and what answers it
